correctness.rationale: Every budget-one candidate is upper bounded by the centered-edge-length Rayleigh trace certificate. For both price branches, the explicitly constructed centered embedding attains all edge lengths and the exact claimed total squared norm, and its unscaled optimal Laplacian has those embedding coordinates as eigenvalue-one vectors. On the low-price side, a principal submatrix of L-I is positive semidefinite, forcing exactly one eigenvalue below one by interlacing; on the high-price side the leaf-eliminated two-by-two Schur complement has inertia (negative,zero), forcing a unique eigenvalue below one and a simple second eigenvalue. Equality conditions at individual leaves determine every spoke rate and the budget determines the bridge rate. A standalone standard-library checker passed 299 exact-rational low/high/boundary cases. Quantified proof is algebraic, not inferred from computation; no independent audit.

value.rationale: The double-star is the smallest nontrivial hub-and-spoke topology with an intercluster bottleneck; a separate bridge price naturally arises in budgeted network design. The result characterizes the exact optimal spectral gap and each individual edge rate for all asymmetric leaf sizes and all positive real bridge prices, and discovers a genuine threshold in eigenvalue multiplicity (and a second-derivative kink). This parametric classification has mathematical utility beyond numerical SDP solvability and beyond the previously solved single unit-price case; its scope and residual literature risk are explicitly delimited.
